statement: Assume every activity has period ω under common field translations, and its field dependence lies in the sites of its occupied support X together with a fixed microscopic collar of width at most a fixed small fraction of u. The norm padding Du(X) is generally larger. Call an input small when its connected support has |X| ≤ nsm, for the fixed block threshold of the calculus. For a linear direction assume the point bound |F|u,X,ϕ ≤ νXWκ u (X, ϕ)eVu(X,ϕ) for every real ϕ, with νX < ∞; the resulting estimates are homogeneous in νX. For a sufficiently large fixed dyadic L, sufficiently large weights Aw, and a sufficiently small activity ball, shell integration and designated localizations on small linear inputs give the exact identity EζZu(K; ϕ + ζ) = Y B∈BLu (1 + aB) ZLu(K′ ; ϕ). (44) The map is analytic in the activities. If the total input size, including separately measured singleton coefficients, is ν, its nonlinear remainder is bounded by CL,Aw ν2, with the corresponding differentiated bounds. A residual from a large input retains its whole coarse closure; only a piece from a small linear input can be assigned to a singleton. The coefficient aB is the complete sum of the field-independent pieces designated at B. Any undesignated constant value of a translated nonconstant piece remains in K′. Write Γu = C<Lu − C<u for the shell from u to Lu. For its estimates on the aligned block and observation grids of a finite square or torus of side M, assume Lu ≤ M/D0, with D0 a sufficiently large fixed range buffer. The norms (41)–(43) have the shell composition, localization, charge, and large-support contractions of [B, Sections 4 and 8, Lemma 9.2]. In particular, the extra regulator is monotone under enlargement, adds on compatible separated supports, and costs C|X| under shell averaging. On the full bulk block grid, a small neutral input invariant under field negation has gain CL−3 after constant and quadratic localization. Removing only the constant gives CL−2 for a neutral input invariant under field negation and CL−1 for a general neutral input, including at irregular end blocks. For a charge-k component of a small input, k ̸= 0, the Gaussian charge gain is exp n − βsh|k|α − 1 2β2 sh  Γu(v0, v0) + h0|k|α o . 23 Here a charge-k component obeys F(ϕ + c) = eikαcF(ϕ), v0 is a reference site in a block of X, and βsh > 0 is the Cameron-shift amplitude. The analytic radius must satisfy h0 > Cshβsh, where Csh is the fixed geometric constant for that shift, and the parameters are chosen so that βshΓu(v0, v0) > h0 by a uniform fixed margin. The displayed gains are then summable over k ̸= 0. This is [B, Equation (4.26)]. Large inputs can be made an arbitrarily small linear contribution by increasing Aw.
